tagline: The FL Players league newsletter · est. 2008
headline: Austin Beats Joey, Anthony Scores 143, and Division 1 Is a Coin Flip
dek: Inside: Joe Burrow's 39.48 for Austin, Anthony's 63-point win over Nase, James at 7-1, the Austin and Brett trade, the back James cut and John started for 33.6, the receiver Nase cut who would have flipped two games, the division races, and every manager's story.
lead:
Monday night had a player in all six games and flipped none of them. Joey came closest: he trailed Austin 135.78 to 89.0 going into Monday, got 34.78 that night, and lost 135.78 to 123.78.

That loss reshaped Division 1. Austin won behind Joe Burrow's 39.48, the best game by any player this week, and Anthony beat Nase 143.08 to 79.86, the high score and the biggest margin of the week. A week ago Joey was 61% to win the division. Now he is 50% and Anthony 46%, a game apart, with Anthony leading the league in points. In Division 2, James won his sixth straight and is 91% to take it.

managers.text: Beat Buckley 103.66 to 88.20 behind Tee Higgins (32.5), Josh Allen (26.56) and T.J. Hockenson (13.8), with 5.00 left on the bench. Drake London started for 1.3. He then claimed Adonai Mitchell for $5, dropping Hockenson, plus the Bears defense for $5 and Tyler Bass for $2. Earlier in the week he cut Tyler Allgeier for Caleb Douglas (see the moves). He shares the lead in the Coach of the year race at 94% lineup efficiency. His two previous 7-1 starts: a lost final in 2016 and a playoff trip in 2022.
managers.next: Week 9: Colt, a rematch of the 2017 final and the game of the week. The series is 8-8, Colt won the last meeting, and James is a 61% favorite.
managers.outlook: A bye 91% of the time, and the best title odds in the league (29%). Second in points (944.70), and two games clear in Division 2.

managers.text: 143.08 against Nase, the high score of the week, and a 63.22-point win, the biggest of the week. Bhayshul Tuten (28.9), Kirk Cousins (28.18) and Chuba Hubbard (21.4) led it. Cousins was a free-agent pickup this week, for Jacoby Brissett, and Brenton Strange, another one, started for 6.5. D'Andre Swift scored 26.9 on the bench. He leads the league in points (966.70) and has beaten Sleeper's projections by 87.1, the most of anyone.
managers.next: Week 9: Scott, a rematch of last year's semifinal, which Anthony won 127.5 to 115.08. Scott leads the series 7-3, and Anthony is a 59% favorite.
managers.outlook: 95% to make the playoffs and 46% to win Division 1, a week after he was at 28%. His one previous 5-3 start, in 2018, made the playoffs.

managers.text: Scored 123.78, well above the median, and lost to Austin by 12.00. Michael Wilson (22.8), Braelon Allen (22.3) and Jaxon Smith-Njigba (20.8) led it, and Rachaad White scored 13.0 on the bench. His kicker, Nick Folk, started and scored 0.0, and a free-agent kicker would have flipped the game (see the moves). He dropped Bo Nix for the Commanders defense, which started for 13.0. Breece Hall is trending toward a return in week 9, the Jets coach said Wednesday.
managers.next: Week 9: Brett. Joey leads the series 13-7, won last year's meeting 85.26 to 84.74, and is a 57% favorite.
managers.outlook: 94% to make the playoffs, and the division is now a coin flip with Anthony. His two previous 6-2 starts both made the playoffs, and the 2020 one won the title.

managers.text: Beat Mikey 99.20 to 89.10, the closest game of the week, while scoring under the median. Kyler Murray (19.9), Puka Nacua (19.5) and Derrick Henry (13.0) led it; Jason Myers started for 3.0 and Jordan Addison scored 10.1 on the bench. Then he cut Murray, who has a sore hamstring, for Kendre Miller, and swapped the Patriots defense for the Packers. He shares the Coach of the year lead with James at 94%.
managers.next: Week 9: James, a rematch of the 2017 final and the game of the week. Colt is at 39%.
managers.outlook: 76% to make the playoffs and second in Division 2, two games behind James. His one previous 5-3 start, in 2015, missed.

managers.text: Beat Joey 135.78 to 123.78, every point of it scored on Sunday. Burrow led it, with Ja'Marr Chase (25.6) and Bucky Irving (21.0); Tre Tucker started and scored 0.0, and Kenny Gainwell had 14.0 on the bench. Burrow has 68.4 points in two starts since the trade with James. He made another trade the night after last week's issue, with Brett (see the moves), and his last three weeks average 112.1, the hottest hand in the league.
managers.next: Week 9: T.J., a rematch of last year's semifinal, which Austin won 103.86 to 101.46. T.J. leads the series 15-8, but Austin has won the last two and is a 53% favorite.
managers.outlook: 27% to make the playoffs. His two previous 3-5 starts split: 2014 missed, and 2018 won the title.

tags.t: Most points left on the bench

managers.text: Lost 103.66 to 88.20 to James. Lamar Jackson started, hurt his thumb on the Ravens' first play and scored 0.0; he needs surgery and is on injured reserve. One free agent would have flipped the game (see the moves). The Steelers defense (19.0), Trey McBride (16.7) and Luther Burden (15.1) led the lineup, and Emmett Johnson scored 22.8 on the bench, part of 42.02 left there, the worst lineup week anyone has had this season. Jeremiyah Love, from the Austin trade, is on injured reserve for four to five weeks, and A.J. Brown did not practice Wednesday.
managers.next: Week 9: Mikey. Buckley has won the last three meetings, leads the series 11-3 and is a 56% favorite.
managers.outlook: 51% to make the playoffs. His four previous 4-4 starts (2012, 2013, 2020, 2022) all missed.

managers.text: Beat T.J. 104.40 to 78.28 behind Josh Jacobs (20.2), Trevor Lawrence (19.4) and Jonah Coleman (18.4), the $35 claim. Parker Washington, from the Austin trade, started for 3.1, and Rashee Rice scored 14.8 on the bench. 20 adds this season, and his waiver pickups have started for 194.1 points, the most in the league. Loveland and Coleman are both off in week 10.
managers.outlook: 35% to make the playoffs. His three previous 4-4 starts: the 2013 title, a 2016 miss and a 2022 playoff trip.

managers.text: Lost 143.08 to 79.86 to Anthony. Harold Fannin (18.4), DeMario Douglas (15.1) and Rome Odunze (10.7) led it; the Broncos defense started for 2.0, and DJ Moore had 14.6 on the bench. He picked up Douglas during the week for Adonai Mitchell, and Mitchell, unrostered, scored 23.7 (see the moves). Eleventh in points.
managers.next: Week 9: John, a Division 1 game. John leads the series 11-10, and Nase is at 41%.
managers.outlook: 28% to make the playoffs and 1% to win the division. Last year's 4-4 start missed.

managers.text: Scored 113.44, above the median, and lost to John by 11.92. Patrick Mahomes (25.44), Jahmyr Gibbs (23.8) and Matthew Golden (17.4) led it; George Pickens scored 5.8 and the Seahawks defense 2.0, and Ryan Flournoy, added during the week, had 11.6 on the bench. He also added Khalil Shakir and Xavier Worthy. Third in points (885.84) and above the median in six of eight weeks, but 3-5 for the first time in his history here.
managers.next: Week 9: Anthony, a rematch of last year's semifinal. Scott leads the series 7-3 and is at 41%.
managers.outlook: 43% to make the playoffs, the scoring keeping him in it.

managers.text: Beat Scott 125.36 to 113.44 without a point left on the bench. Tyler Allgeier, a free-agent pickup that week, scored 33.6, with Drake Maye (22.46) and the Bucs defense (18.0), another pickup, behind him. Omar Cooper started and scored 0.0. Allgeier should keep Arizona's backfield for now, with Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve. He also claimed Michael Mayer, dropping Alec Pierce.
managers.next: Week 9: Nase, a Division 1 game. John is a 59% favorite.
managers.outlook: 31% to make the playoffs. His three previous 3-5 starts: a 2013 playoff trip, and misses in 2018 and 2022.

managers.text: 78.28 against Brett, the lowest score of the week. Brock Bowers (24.7), Jayden Daniels (14.98) and Christian Watson (13.3) led it; the Chiefs defense started for 0.0 and Wan'Dale Robinson had 12.7 on the bench. He claimed Dylan Sampson for $8, dropping Roschon Johnson. Players he brought in by trade or off the wire have started for 304.1 points, the most in the league, with Jared Goff still the pickup of the year at 86.8 in four starts. De'Von Achane is still on injured reserve.
managers.next: Week 9: Austin, a rematch of last year's semifinal. T.J. leads the series 15-8 and is at 47%.
managers.outlook: 18% to make the playoffs. He is second in the board duty race at 14%. His two previous 3-5 starts (2016, 2023) both missed.

managers.text: Lost the closest game of the week to Colt, 99.20 to 89.10. Tony Pollard (27.2), Dak Prescott (19.8) and Tucker Kraft (14.3) led it; Zay Flowers started and scored 0.0 with no catches, and one free agent would have flipped it (see the moves). He added kicker Cam Little for the Ravens defense. Saquon Barkley says the Eagles told him he will not be traded.
managers.next: Week 9: Buckley, who has won the last three meetings. Mikey is at 44%.
managers.outlook: 1% to make the playoffs: none of the 11 teams in league history to start 1-7 got in. He is 70% to finish last and 27% for board duty, the highest in the league; board duty goes to the loser of the losers bracket.

trends.title: What eight weeks means here
trends.text: The one 8-0 team in league history made the playoffs. 7-1 teams made it 7 times in 8, 6-2 teams 93% of the time, 5-3 teams 75%, 4-4 teams 49%, 3-5 teams 31% and 2-6 teams 7%.

trends.title: Scoring
trends.text: Week 8 averaged 107.0 a team, up from 104.3, with a median of 104.03.

trends.title: The kicker file
trends.text: No game was decided by the kickers this week. The two this season are still Joey over John in week 2 and Colt over John in week 7, and John was on the wrong end of both.

history.title: Week 8, all time
history.text: The highest week 8 score on record is James's 183.16 against Buckley in 2019. The biggest week 8 blowout was James over Austin, 139.28 to 50.86, in 2017. The closest was Mikey over Nase, 108.52 to 108.2, in 2024.

ahead: Game of the week: James and Colt, first and second in Division 2, in a rematch of the 2017 final with the series even at 8-8. Also: Joey against Brett and Anthony against Scott, the two Division 1 leaders on the same day, and T.J. against Austin in a rematch of last year's semifinal.

moves.intro: One trade, a running back who changed hands for nothing, and four games the wire would have flipped.

items.title: Austin and Brett
items.text: Austin got Garrett Wilson and Jaylen Warren. Brett got Jadarian Price, Parker Washington and Zach Charbonnet, who came to Austin in the Buckley trade a week earlier. Warren started for 20.8 and Wilson for 11.3; Washington started for Brett and scored 3.1.
items.verdict: Austin's third trade in three weeks.

items.title: Allgeier, cut and started
items.text: James dropped Tyler Allgeier for Caleb Douglas during the week. John picked Allgeier up and started him, and he scored 33.6 in a game John won by 11.92. Douglas scored 6.3 on James's bench.
items.verdict: With Love on injured reserve, John may have Arizona's lead back.

items.title: Adonai Mitchell, two flips
items.text: Nase dropped Mitchell for DeMario Douglas during the week, and Mitchell scored 23.7 unrostered. In for George Pickens he flips Scott's 11.92 loss to John; in for Zay Flowers he flips Mikey's 10.10 loss to Colt. James has since claimed him for $5.
items.verdict: The free agent of the week, now on the team with the best record.

items.title: Two more from the wire
items.text: Cam Ward scored 26.3 unrostered; in for Lamar Jackson, he flips Buckley's 15.46 loss to James. Jason Sanders scored 15.0 unrostered; in for Nick Folk, he flips Joey's 12.00 loss to Austin.
items.verdict: Four flips in week 8, tied with week 3 for the most this season.

features.label: The races
features.title: Two divisions, two byes
features.dek: The byes go to the division winners, not the two best records.

blocks.text: Two weeks ago Anthony was the favorite, last week Joey was, and now it is close to even. Joey has the extra win; Anthony has outscored him by 109.5 points, and the model gives the scoring nearly as much weight. Nobody else in the division is above 2%.
James is two games clear with six to play. Colt is the only team within two games, and he gets James this week.
Chances come from 10,000 simulated finishes of the season after week 8. A tie for a division is broken on points in the model.
No projected starter in the league is on bye. Buckley swapped the Steelers defense for the Lions on Wednesday's waivers.

items: Buckley: Lamar Jackson is on injured reserve and needs thumb surgery. Jeremiyah Love is on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain, out four to five weeks. A.J. Brown did not practice Wednesday.
Colt: TreVeyon Henderson did not practice Wednesday (illness).
Joey: Breece Hall is trending toward a return this week, per the Jets coach.
T.J.: De'Von Achane is still on injured reserve.
Baltimore: Joe Fagnano starts Thursday night after Jackson's injury, and Tyler Huntley is out for the season.
